citations.description: Policy grants bedrock:InvokeModel + bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream on anthropic.claude-* ARNs — the precondition for a successful call, but not evidence the call was made
Ticket 'CORRECTION' comment records from-instance call result with instance ID and role ARN, but criterion is untagged so attestation is not admissible evidence under codebase-verifiable rules

findings.criterion: a real `bedrock-runtime converse` call executed FROM the instance (SSM, as the instance role) returns a model response — the ONLY check that reveals which IAM action the service authorizes against
findings.detail: This criterion is untagged (codebase-verifiable). The codebase cannot contain evidence of a live call result from a running instance. The IAM policy in iam_s7.tf grants the correct actions and resources, but the criterion specifically requires a real call to have been executed and returned a model response — that evidence lives outside the codebase. Ticket comments do record this attestation (the 'CORRECTION' comment names instance i-00880b2c7f13527c5, role assumed-role/rebar-gerrit-instance-role, result 'ready'), but since the criterion is untagged it must be judged by the codebase bar, which cannot be met.
findings.remediation: Tag this criterion [operator-attested] so the ticket-comment attestation (instance i-00880b2c7f13527c5, role assumed-role/rebar-gerrit-instance-role, result 'ready', recorded in the CORRECTION comment) becomes admissible evidence and the criterion can be judged met.

citations.description: Ticket comments reviewed: none records an IMDSv2 token PUT to 169.254.169.254/latest/api/token from inside the review-bot container with the result

findings.criterion: [operator-attested] AC1: an IMDSv2 token request from inside the review-bot container is executed and its result recorded as a comment on this ticket, selecting either the IAM-only path or the hop-limit contingency
findings.detail: No ticket comment records the IMDSv2 token PUT result from inside the review-bot container. The criterion requires the probe result to be recorded as a comment. The ticket comments record from-instance Converse call results (implying IMDS was reachable) but never explicitly record the AC1 IMDS probe output. The concrete-attestation bar for operator-attested criteria requires a named observed outcome; no such comment exists.
findings.remediation: Record the IMDSv2 probe result as a ticket comment: run `curl -s -X PUT -H 'X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds: 21600' http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token` from inside compose-review-bot-1, paste the output (token or error), and note which path (IAM-only or hop-limit contingency) was selected.

citations.description: Ticket comments reviewed: the CORRECTION comment records identity via boto3 STS call inside the streaming script, but no standalone `aws sts get-caller-identity` output with confirmation of no access key in environment is recorded

findings.criterion: [operator-attested] `aws sts get-caller-identity` from inside the review-bot container returns `rebar-gerrit-instance-role`, with no AWS access key present in the container environment (command output in a ticket comment)
findings.detail: No ticket comment records the `aws sts get-caller-identity` output from inside the review-bot container. The criterion explicitly requires the command output to be in a ticket comment. The 'CORRECTION' comment records the identity as part of the streaming verification (IDENTITY: arn:aws:sts::896586841071:assumed-role/rebar-gerrit-instance-role/i-00880b2c7f13527c5) but this is from a boto3 script, not `aws sts get-caller-identity`, and does not confirm the absence of an AWS access key in the container environment.
findings.remediation: Run `aws sts get-caller-identity` from inside compose-review-bot-1 and `env | grep AWS_ACCESS_KEY` (expecting no output), then record both outputs as a ticket comment.

citations.description: Ticket comments reviewed: none records container health output for opcert SSM fetch or Gerrit startup after the S7 apply

findings.criterion: `opcert` SSM fetch and Gerrit startup both still succeed after apply, evidenced by container health output
findings.detail: No ticket comment records container health output for opcert or Gerrit after the apply. The criterion requires health output as evidence. The ticket comments discuss the apply and verification of Bedrock access but do not include docker health check output or equivalent evidence for opcert and Gerrit.
findings.remediation: Record container health output as a ticket comment: `docker inspect --format='{{.State.Health.Status}}' compose-opcert-1 compose-gerrit-1` (or equivalent), confirming both are healthy after the apply.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: for each one, decide whether the work is genuinely incomplete or simply undocumented. If a requirement is already satisfied but the proof is not discoverable from the code alone, add a comment to this ticket that documents the evidence — cite the concrete artifacts that meet the requirement (file paths and line ranges, commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the work to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. For any criterion whose work is genuinely unfinished, complete it, then re-verify.
